sections.text: Start with first quarter. Compare its bright half with the full Moon.
Moonlight is sunlight bouncing off the Moon. As the Moon travels around Earth, we see different amounts of its lit half. From one new Moon to the next takes about 29½ days.

sections.prompt: Choose a stage. Compare its bright edge with the stage before it.

stages.description: The sunlit half faces away from Earth. The Moon is usually invisible to us at this stage.
stages.imageAlt: Dark lunar disk at new Moon.
stages.label: New Moon

stages.description: A bright sliver appears. Over the next few nights we see more of the sunlit half.
stages.imageAlt: Thin curved sliver of the lunar disk illuminated.
stages.label: Waxing crescent

stages.description: About a quarter of the cycle has passed. The bright area fills half the disk we see.
stages.imageAlt: Half of the visible lunar disk is bright.
stages.label: First quarter

stages.description: More than half the disk looks bright, and the bright part is still growing.
stages.imageAlt: A mostly bright disk with a narrow dark edge.
stages.label: Waxing gibbous

stages.description: Earth faces nearly the entire sunlit half. A full Moon rises around sunset.
stages.label: Full Moon

stages.description: More than half the disk still looks bright. Now the bright part grows smaller each night.
stages.imageAlt: A mostly illuminated Moon after full.
stages.label: Waning gibbous

stages.description: Half of the disk looks bright again. Compare the bright side with first quarter.
stages.imageAlt: Half-lit disk with the opposite side bright from first quarter.
stages.label: Third quarter

stages.description: Only a thin sliver looks bright before the next new Moon.
stages.imageAlt: Thin crescent of sunlight before new Moon.
stages.label: Waning crescent

sections.text: Find sunlight entering the diagram. Compare the Moon’s position in its orbit with the shape a person on Earth sees.

Six words for a Moon watcher
Orbit — a path around another object.
Phase — the shape of the bright part we see.
Crescent — a curved sliver.
Gibbous — more than half of the disk looks bright.
Waxing — the bright part is growing.
Waning — the bright part is shrinking.
Trace the Moon’s path in the diagram with your finger. Stop twice where the disk looks half bright. What changes between the two views?
